1063+open StlcCommon
1064+open Lean Meta Elab Term

1066+def language : Language where
1067+  tyType := ``Ty
1068+  tmType := ``Tm
1069+  arrowCtor := ``Ty.arrow
1070+  varCtor := ``Tm.var
1071+  appCtor := ``Tm.app
1072+  absCtor := ``Tm.abs
1073+  -- defined later
1074+  subst := `StlcExtended.subst
1075+  hasType := `StlcExtended.HasType

1077+def extendedTyHandler : TyElabHandler :=
1078+  fun recur k T => do
1079+    match T with
1080+    | `(stlcTy| Nat) =>
1081+        return mkConst ``Ty.nat
1082+    | `(stlcTy| Unit) =>
1083+        return mkConst ``Ty.unit
1084+    | `(stlcTy| $T₁:stlcTy + $T₂:stlcTy) => do
1085+        let T₁ ← recur T₁
1086+        let T₂ ← recur T₂
1087+        return mkApp2 (mkConst ``Ty.sum) T₁ T₂
1088+    | `(stlcTy| [$T:stlcTy]) => do
1089+        let T ← recur T
1090+        return mkApp (mkConst ``Ty.list) T
1091+    | `(stlcTy| $T₁:stlcTy × $T₂:stlcTy) => do
1092+        let T₁ ← recur T₁
1093+        let T₂ ← recur T₂
1094+        return mkApp2 (mkConst ``Ty.prod) T₁ T₂
1095+    | _ => k T
1096+
1097+def tyHandlers : TyElabHandler :=
1098+  extendedTyHandler.orElse (commonTyHandler language)
1099+
1100+partial def elabTy : TyElab :=
1101+  tyHandlers elabTy <| unsupportedTy language
1102+
1103+def extendedTmHandler : TmElabHandler :=
1104+  fun recur k Γ free t => do
1105+    match t with
1106+    | `(stlcTm| $n:num) => do
1107+        return (mkApp (mkConst ``Tm.const) (mkNatLit n.getNat), free )
1108+
1109+    | `(stlcTm| Nat) => do
1110+        throwError "`Nat` is not a valid term."
1111+
1112+    | `(stlcTm| succ $t:stlcTm) => do
1113+        let (t, free) ← recur Γ free t
1114+        return (mkApp (mkConst ``Tm.succ) t, free)
1115+
1116+    | `(stlcTm| pred $t:stlcTm) => do
1117+        let (t, free) ← recur Γ free t
1118+        return (mkApp (mkConst ``Tm.pred) t, free)
1119+
1120+    | `(stlcTm| $t₁:stlcTm * $t₂:stlcTm) => do
1121+        let (t₁, free) ← recur Γ free t₁
1122+        let (t₂, free) ← recur Γ free t₂
1123+        return (mkApp2 (mkConst ``Tm.mult) t₁ t₂, free)
1124+
1125+    | `(stlcTm| if0 $c:stlcTm then $t:stlcTm else $e:stlcTm) => do
1126+        let (c, free) ← recur Γ free c
1127+        let (t, free) ← recur Γ free t
1128+        let (e, free) ← recur Γ free e
1129+        return (mkApp3 (mkConst ``Tm.ite0) c t e, free)
1130+
1131+    | `(stlcTm| inl $T:stlcTy $t:stlcTm) => do
1132+        let T ← elabTy T
1133+        let (t, free) ← recur Γ free t
1134+        return (mkApp2 (mkConst ``Tm.sumInl) T t, free)
1135+
1136+    | `(stlcTm| inr $T:stlcTy $t:stlcTm) => do
1137+        let T ← elabTy T
1138+        let (t, free) ← recur Γ free t
1139+        return (mkApp2 (mkConst ``Tm.sumInr) T t, free)
1140+
1141+    | `(stlcTm|
1142+        case $t:stlcTm of
1143+          inl $x₁:stlcVar => $t₁:stlcTm |
1144+          inr $x₂:stlcVar => $t₂:stlcTm) => do
1145+
1146+        let (t, free) ← recur Γ free t
1147+
1148+        -- The branches start from the same lexical Γ
1149+        -- Only `free` is threaded from branch 1 into branch 2
1150+        let (x₁, Γ₁) ← elabStlcBinder language Γ x₁
1151+        let (t₁, free) ← recur Γ₁ free t₁
1152+
1153+        let (x₂, Γ₂) ← elabStlcBinder language Γ x₂
1154+        let (t₂, free) ← recur Γ₂ free t₂
1155+
1156+        return (mkAppN (mkConst ``Tm.sumCase) #[t, x₁, t₁, x₂, t₂], free)
1157+
1158+    | `(stlcTm| nil $T:stlcTy) => do
1159+        let T ← elabTy T
1160+        return (mkApp (mkConst ``Tm.listNil) T, free)
1161+
1162+    | `(stlcTm| $t₁:stlcTm :: $t₂:stlcTm) => do
1163+        let (t₁, free) ← recur Γ free t₁
1164+        let (t₂, free) ← recur Γ free t₂
1165+        return (mkApp2 (mkConst ``Tm.listCons) t₁ t₂,  free)
1166+
1167+    | `(stlcTm|
1168+        case $t₁:stlcTm of
1169+          nil => $t₂:stlcTm |
1170+          $x:stlcVar :: $xs:stlcVar => $t₃:stlcTm) => do
1171+
1172+        let (t₁, free) ← recur Γ free t₁
1173+
1174+        -- nil branch has no binders
1175+        let (t₂, free) ← recur Γ free t₂
1176+
1177+        -- cons branch has two binders
1178+        let (x, Γ) ← elabStlcBinder language Γ x
1179+        let (xs, Γ) ← elabStlcBinder language Γ xs
1180+
1181+        let (t₃, free) ← recur Γ free t₃
1182+
1183+        return (mkAppN (mkConst ``Tm.listCase) #[t₁, t₂, x, xs, t₃], free)
1184+
1185+    | `(stlcTm| Unit) => do
1186+        throwError "`Unit` is not a valid term."
1187+
1188+    | `(stlcTm| unit) => do
1189+        return (mkConst ``Tm.unit, free)
1190+
1191+    | `(stlcTm| ($t₁:stlcTm, $t₂:stlcTm)) => do
1192+        let (t₁, free) ← recur Γ free t₁
1193+        let (t₂, free) ← recur Γ free t₂
1194+        return (mkApp2 (mkConst ``Tm.pair) t₁ t₂, free)
1195+
1196+    | `(stlcTm| fst $t:stlcTm) => do
1197+        let (t, free) ← recur Γ free t
1198+        return (mkApp (mkConst ``Tm.fst) t, free)
1199+
1200+    | `(stlcTm| snd $t:stlcTm) => do
1201+        let (t, free) ← recur Γ free t
1202+        return (mkApp (mkConst ``Tm.snd) t, free)
1203+
1204+    | `(stlcTm|
1205+        let $x:stlcVar = $t₁:stlcTm
1206+        in $t₂:stlcTm) => do
1207+
1208+        -- x is NOT in scope in t₁
1209+        let (t₁, free) ← recur Γ free t₁
1210+
1211+        -- but in scope in t₂
1212+        let (x, Γ₂) ← elabStlcBinder language Γ x
1213+
1214+        let (t₂, free) ← recur Γ₂ free t₂
1215+
1216+        return (mkApp3 (mkConst ``Tm.letIn) x t₁ t₂, free)
1217+
1218+    | `(stlcTm| fix $t:stlcTm) => do
1219+        let (t, free) ← recur Γ free t
1220+        return (mkApp (mkConst ``Tm.fix) t, free)
1221+
1222+    | _ => k Γ free t
1223+
1224+def tmHandlers : TmElabHandler :=
1225+  extendedTmHandler.orElse (commonTmHandler language elabTy)
1226+
1227+
1228+partial def elabTm : TmElab :=
1229+  tmHandlers elabTm unsupportedTm
1230+
1231+def elabCtx : CtxElab := elabCtxCommon language elabTy
1232+
1233+@[scoped term_elab StlcCommon.bracket]
1234+def elabBracket : TermElab :=
1235+  fun stx expectedType? => do
1236+    let `(<{ $q:stlcQuoted }>) := stx
1237+      | throwUnsupportedSyntax
1238+    elabQuoted language elabTy elabTm elabCtx q expectedType?
1239+

1249+@[app_unexpander Ty.nat]
1250+private def Ty.unexpandNat : Unexpander
1251+  | stx => do
1252+    let Nat := mkObjectIdentFrom stx "Nat"
1253+    let T ← `(stlcTy| $Nat:ident)
1254+    `(<{ $T:stlcTy }>)
1255+
1256+@[app_unexpander Ty.unit]
1257+private def Ty.unexpandUnit : Unexpander
1258+  | stx => do
1259+    let Unit := mkObjectIdentFrom stx "Unit"
1260+    let T ← `(stlcTy| $Unit:ident)
1261+    `(<{ $T:stlcTy }>)
1262+
1263+@[app_unexpander Ty.arrow]
1264+private def Ty.unexpandArrow : Unexpander := Delab.unexpandArrow
1265+
1266+@[app_unexpander Ty.sum]
1267+private def Ty.unexpandSum : Unexpander
1268+  | `($_ $T₁ $T₂) => do
1269+      let T₁' := getTy T₁
1270+      let T₂' := getTy T₂
1271+      `(<{ $T₁':stlcTy + $T₂':stlcTy }>)
1272+  | _ => throw ()
1273+
1274+
1275+@[app_unexpander Ty.list]
1276+private def Ty.unexpandList : Unexpander
1277+  | `($_ $T) => do
1278+      let T' := getTy T
1279+      `(<{ [$T':stlcTy] }>)
1280+  | _ => throw ()
1281+
1282+@[app_unexpander Ty.prod]
1283+private def Ty.unexpandProd : Unexpander
1284+  | `($_ $T₁ $T₂) => do

218+--  The constructors above give us a precise representation of STLC syntax,
219+--  but expressions written directly with them quickly become hard to read.
220220 --  We need some notation magic to set up the concrete syntax, as we did in
221221 --  the Types chapter...
222222 --
223---  The upshot of this section is that STLC types and terms are both
224---  written inside one pair of brackets, `<{ … }>`, and that `~e` inside
225---  the brackets escapes back to an arbitrary Lean expression:
226---  - `<{ Bool → Bool }>` is a type;
227---  - `<{ λ x : Bool . x }>` is a term — a bare identifier inside the
228---    brackets is the object-language variable of that name, so `<{ x }>`
229---    is the variable `x`;
230---  - `<{ ~t₁ ~t₂ }>` applies one Lean-level term to another.
231---
232---  Lean works out from context which of the two a given bracket holds, so
233---  the same brackets serve for types, for terms, and — when we come to
234---  typing — for typing judgments too. How that works is in the collapsed
235---  blocks below; nothing later in the chapter depends on it.
236-
237---  THE FOLLOWING DETAILS CAN BE SKIPPED (Notation encoding: types)
238---  The `stlcTy` grammar covers `Bool`, arrows (written `→` or `->`,
239---  associating to the right), parentheses, and `~e`. A bare identifier
240---  other than `Bool` is spliced in as a Lean term, so a local `T` — or any
241---  Lean expression of type `Ty` — can appear directly inside the brackets.
242---
243---  To extend the grammar, a later chapter adds a `syntax` line to the
244---  category and a matching `macro_rules` case; that is all it takes to add
245---  a new type construct.
246-

272---  THE FOLLOWING DETAILS CAN BE SKIPPED (Notation encoding: terms)
273---  Terms are built from variables, application (associating to the left),
274---  abstraction, the two boolean constants, and conditionals. A binding
275---  occurrence — the `x` in `λ x : T . t` — has a small grammar of its own,
276---  `stlcVar`, and `varStr` turns it into the string that `Tm.abs` stores.
277---
278---  Because types and terms share the brackets, each `macro_rules` group
279---  says which bracket it belongs to (`kind := tyBracket`,
280---  `kind := tmBracket`), and each antiquote in a nested quotation says
281---  which grammar it came from. A bare identifier is the one genuinely
282---  overlapping case: `Bool` in term position would otherwise quietly
283---  become a variable named `Bool`, so that rule rejects it, which also
284---  settles which grammar a lone `<{ Bool }>` belongs to.
285---
286---  The last production, `[x := s] t`, is the notation for substitution; we
287---  give it its meaning when we define substitution below. It binds tighter
288---  than application, so `[x:=s] t₁ t₂` is the application of `[x:=s] t₁`
289---  to `t₂`, and a `λ` or `if` body must be parenthesized:
290---  `[x:=s] (λ y : Bool . x)`.

223+--  We will write STLC syntax inside `<{ ... }>` brackets. For example,
224+--  `<{ λ X : Bool . X }>` represents the term
225+--  `Tm.abs "X" Ty.bool (Tm.var "X")`.
226+--
227+--  This notation must also support definitions and proofs about
228+--  **arbitrary** piece of STLC syntax. For example, a theorem may
229+--  introduce Lean variables `t : Tm` and `τ : Ty`, representing an
230+--  arbitrary STLC term and type. Inside the brackets, we can then write
231+--  `<{ λ X : τ . t }>`. Here `X` is the name of a variable in the STLC
232+--  term being represented, while `τ` and `t` refer to the Lean variables
233+--  in the surrounding theorem.
234+--
235+--  The notation distinguishes these two uses by naming convention, which
236+--  we will follow throughout the STLC chapters:
237+--  - A name beginning with a capital Latin letter is taken literally as a
238+--    name in the STLC syntax. Thus `X`, `Y`, and `Zed` are STLC term
239+--    variables. Such a name must be a single Lean identifier and cannot
240+--    contain a dot. In languages with named base types, which we will see
241+--    in the Sub chapter, names such as `A`, `Int`, and `Bool` name those
242+--    types.
243+--  - A name beginning with a lowercase letter or a Greek letter refers to
244+--    a Lean variable in the surrounding definition or proof. This lets us
245+--    use the usual names `x` and `y` for strings, `t` and `u` for terms,
246+--    `τ` for types, and `Γ` for contexts without additional punctuation.
247+--  - To insert a larger Lean expression, prefix it with `~`. For example,
248+--    `<{ ~(Tm.var "X") t }>` inserts the expression `Tm.var "X"` as the
249+--    function and the Lean variable `t` as its argument. The same escape
250+--    is needed to insert a capitalized Lean variable, since an unescaped
251+--    capitalized name is taken literally as an STLC name.
252+--
253+--  This capitalization convention applies to actual variable names in
254+--  concrete STLC examples and inside `<{ ... }>` brackets. In grammars,
255+--  inference rules, and general explanations, symbols such as `x`, `t`,
256+--  and `T` instead stand for an arbitrary variable name, term, or type. We
257+--  keep the conventional lowercase notation for these schematic symbols.
258+

284+    | _ => k T

286+def tyHandlers : TyElabHandler :=

288+
289+partial def elabTy : TyElab :=

291+
292+def boolTmHandler : TmElabHandler :=
293+  fun recur k Γ free t => do
294+    match t with
295+    | `(stlcTm| true) => do
296+        return (mkConst ``Tm.tru, free)
297+    | `(stlcTm| false) => do
298+        return (mkConst ``Tm.fls, free)
299+    | `(stlcTm| Bool) => do
300+        throwError "`Bool` is not a valid term."
301+    | `(stlcTm| if $c:stlcTm then $t:stlcTm else $e:stlcTm) => do
302+        let (c, free) ← recur Γ free c
303+        let (t, free) ← recur Γ free t
304+        let (e, free) ← recur Γ free e
305+        return (mkApp3 (mkConst ``Tm.ite) c t e, free)
306+    | _ => k Γ free t
307+
308+def tmHandlers : TmElabHandler :=
309+  boolTmHandler.orElse (commonTmHandler language elabTy)
310+
311+partial def elabTm : TmElab :=
312+  tmHandlers elabTm unsupportedTm
313+
314+def elabCtx : CtxElab := elabCtxCommon language elabTy

100+/-!
101+Trick: resolve the forward-referenced `hasType` here
102+so that `HasType` notation is aviable when defining `HasType`.
103+This relies on Lean's `inductive` elabrator implementation detail:
104+an auxiliary fvar of the inductive type being defined is created
105+before the consturctors are elaborated to represent this inductive type,
106+because the constructors need to refer the inductive type.
107+So once we resolve `HasType`, that auxiliary fvar is correctly used.
108+I (berberman) think this is better than macro-based notation with `set_option hygiene false`.
109+-/
110+def Language.mkHasType (lang : Language) (Γ t T : Expr) : TermElabM Expr := do
111+  let some hasType ← resolveId? (mkIdent lang.hasType)
112+    | throwError "unknown declaration `{lang.hasType}`"
113+  return mkApp3 hasType Γ t T

158+inductive IdentRole where
159+  | term
160+  | type
161+  | name
162+  | context
163+  deriving Repr, BEq

165+def IdentRole.desc : IdentRole → String
166+  | term => "term"
167+  | type => "type"
168+  | name => "name"
169+  | context => "context"
170+
171+inductive IndentKind where
172+  | object
173+  | metavar
174+  deriving Repr, BEq

176+def isGreek (c : Char) : Bool :=
177+  let n := c.val.toNat
178+  decide (
179+    -- Greek and Coptic
180+    (0x0370 ≤ n ∧ n ≤ 0x03ff) ∨
181+    -- Greek Extended
182+    (0x1f00 ≤ n ∧ n ≤ 0x1fff)
183+  )
184+
185+def classifyIdent? (id : Ident) :
186+    Option (IndentKind × String) := do
187+  let Name.str .anonymous s ← id.getId.eraseMacroScopes
188+    | failure
189+  -- reject «a.b»
190+  if s.isEmpty || s.contains '.' then
191+    failure
192+  let c := s.front
193+  if c.isUpper then
194+    return (.object, s)
195+  else if c.isLower || isGreek c then
196+    return (.metavar, s)
197+  else failure
198+
199+def resolveMetaIdent (lang : Language) (role : IdentRole)
200+    (expectedType : Expr) (id : Ident) : TermElabM Expr := do
201+
202+  let some (.metavar, name) := classifyIdent? id
203+    | throwErrorAt id "expected a metalanguage identifier"
204+
205+  -- Used only by error branches
206+  let getCandidates := do
207+    let mut result := #[]
208+    for decl in (← getLCtx) do
209+      unless decl.isImplementationDetail do
210+        if ← withNewMCtxDepth <|
211+            isDefEq decl.type expectedType then
212+          result := result.push decl
213+    return result
214+
215+  -- Give one obvious local-variable replacement
216+  let suggestCandidate (decl : LocalDecl) : TermElabM Unit := do
217+    let candidate := mkIdentFrom id decl.userName.eraseMacroScopes
218+    let term : Term := ⟨candidate.raw⟩
219+
220+    -- quote the Lean variable if its name is in the form of object language variable name
221+    let bare :=
222+      match classifyIdent? candidate with
223+      | some (.metavar, _) => true
224+      | _ => false
225+
226+    let suggestion ←
227+      match role with
228+      | .term =>
229+          if bare then
230+            `(stlcTm| $candidate:ident)
231+          else
232+            `(stlcTm| ~$term)
233+      | .type =>
234+          if bare then
235+            `(stlcTy| $candidate:ident)
236+          else
237+            `(stlcTy| ~$term)
238+      | .name =>
239+          if bare then
240+            `(stlcVar| $candidate:ident)
241+          else
242+            `(stlcVar| ~$term)
243+      | .context =>
244+          if bare then
245+            `(stlcCtx| $candidate:ident)
246+          else
247+            `(stlcCtx| ~$term)
248+
249+    addSuggestion id { suggestion }
250+
251+  -- Main logic starts here
252+  let some e ← resolveId? id (withInfo := false)
253+    | -- we failed to find `id`
254+      do
255+        let candidates ← getCandidates
256+
257+        if let some candidate := candidates[0]? then
258+          suggestCandidate candidate
259+
260+        match role with
261+        | .name =>
262+            let s : Term := ⟨Syntax.mkStrLit name⟩
263+            let suggestion ← `(stlcVar| ~$s)
264+            addSuggestion id { suggestion }
265+        | .term =>
266+            let var : Term := mkIdent lang.varCtor
267+            let s : Term := ⟨Syntax.mkStrLit name⟩
268+            let app ← `($var $s)
269+            let suggestion ← `(stlcTm| ~$app)
270+            addSuggestion id { suggestion }
271+        | .type | .context => pure ()
272+
273+        throwErrorAt id m!"unknown metalanguage {role.desc} identifier `{name}`"
274+
275+  -- we found `id`
276+  let actualType ← inferType e
277+
278+  -- add back if we want to only accept local variable but not global constant
279+  -- unless e.isFVar do
280+  --   let term : Term := ⟨id.raw⟩
281+  --   let suggestion : SuggestionText ←
282+  --     match role with
283+  --     | .term => `(stlcTm| ~$term)
284+  --     | .type => `(stlcTy| ~$term)
285+  --     | .name => `(stlcVar| ~$term)
286+  --     | .context => `(stlcCtx| ~$term)
287+
288+  --   addSuggestion id { suggestion }
289+
290+  --   throwErrorAt id m!"\
291+  --   `{name}` resolves to a Lean declaration, not a local {role.desc} variable; \
292+  --   use `~{name}`"
293+
294+  -- Actual elaboration
295+  if ← commitWhen <| isDefEq actualType expectedType then
296+    addTermInfo' id e
297+    return e
298+
299+  -- Diagnostics only from here on
300+  let actualType ← instantiateMVars actualType
301+  let expectedType ← instantiateMVars expectedType
302+
303+  let candidates ← getCandidates
304+
305+  if let some candidate := candidates[0]? then
306+    suggestCandidate candidate
307+
308+  -- special check for cases like `fun (x : String) => <{ λ x : τ . x }>`:
309+  -- the occurrence of `x` is syntactically meta, but Lean variable `x` is a `String` instead of `Tm`
310+  if role == .term &&  (← withNewMCtxDepth <| isDefEq actualType (mkConst ``String)) then
311+    let var : Term := mkIdent lang.varCtor
312+    let x : Term := ⟨id.raw⟩
313+    let app ← `($var $x)
314+    let suggestion ← `(stlcTm| ~$app)
315+    addSuggestion id { suggestion }
316+
317+  if role == .name then
318+    let s : Term := ⟨Syntax.mkStrLit name⟩
319+    let suggestion ← `(stlcVar| ~$s)
320+    addSuggestion id { suggestion }
321+
322+  throwErrorAt id m!"\
323+  metalanguage {role.desc} identifier `{name}` has type
324+    {actualType}
325+  but this position expects
326+    {expectedType}"
327+
328+def elabStlcVarName (lang : Language) (x : TSyntax `stlcVar) : TermElabM Expr := do
329+  match x with
330+  | `(stlcVar| ~$e:term) =>
331+      elabTermEnsuringType e (mkConst ``String)
332+  | `(stlcVar| $id:ident) =>
333+      match classifyIdent? id with
334+      | some (.object, name) => return mkStrLit name
335+      | some (.metavar, _) =>
336+          resolveMetaIdent lang .name (mkConst ``String) id
337+      | none => throwErrorAt id "\
338+invalid bare name
339+
340+Use an uppercase Latin identifier for an object-language name, \
341+a lowercase/Greek identifier for a Lean String variable, or \
342+explicit `~...` for a Lean expression."
343+  | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax
344+
345+def elabStlcBinder
346+    (lang : Language)
347+    (Γ : Scope)
348+    (x : TSyntax `stlcVar) :
349+    TermElabM (Expr × Scope) := do
350+  match x with
351+  | `(stlcVar| ~$e:term) => do
352+      let name ← elabTermEnsuringType e (mkConst ``String)
353+      return (name, Γ)
354+  | `(stlcVar| $id:ident) =>
355+      match classifyIdent? id with
356+      | some (.object, name) => do
357+          -- Static object binder.
358+          let binding ← mkBinder lang id
359+          return (mkStrLit name, binding :: Γ)
360+      | some (.metavar, _) => do
361+          -- Lean String variable: dynamic binder name.
362+          let name ← resolveMetaIdent lang .name (mkConst ``String) id
363+          return (name, Γ)
364+      | none => throwErrorAt id "\
365+invalid bare binder name
366+
367+Use an uppercase Latin identifier for a static object-language binder, \
368+a lowercase/Greek identifier for a Lean String variable, or \
369+explicit `~...` for an arbitrary Lean name expression."
370+
371+  | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax
372+
373+/-!
374+Two different continuations:
375+* `recur` elaborates a child using the complete language.
376+* `k` continues with the next handler when this handler does not recognize
377+  the current syntax node.
378+-/
379+
380+abbrev TyElab := TSyntax `stlcTy → TermElabM Expr
381+
382+abbrev TyElabHandler := (recur : TyElab) → (k : TyElab) → TyElab
383+
384+abbrev TmElab :=
385+  Scope →
386+  FVars →
387+  TSyntax `stlcTm →
388+  TermElabM (Expr × FVars)
389+
390+abbrev TmElabHandler := (recur : TmElab) → (k : TmElab) → TmElab
391+
392+def TyElabHandler.orElse
393+    (first second : TyElabHandler) :
394+    TyElabHandler :=
395+  fun recur k => first recur (second recur k)
396+
397+def TmElabHandler.orElse
398+    (first second : TmElabHandler) :
399+    TmElabHandler :=
400+  fun recur k => first recur (second recur k)
401+
402+def unsupportedTy (lang : Language) : TyElab :=
403+  fun T => do
404+    match T with
405+    | `(stlcTy| $id:ident) =>
406+        match classifyIdent? id with
407+        | some (.object, name) => do
408+            -- All handlers declined this uppercase identifier.
409+            -- Before throwing unknown object type error, check whether there
410+            -- happens to be a same-named Lean local of the target `Ty` type
411+            -- to give a useful diagnostic for `T : Ty`.
412+            let e? ← resolveId? id (withInfo := false)
413+            if let some e := e? then
414+              if e.isFVar then
415+                let actualType ← inferType e
416+                if ← withNewMCtxDepth <| isDefEq actualType (mkConst lang.tyType) then
417+                  let term : Term := ⟨id.raw⟩
418+                  let suggestion ← `(stlcTy| ~$term)
419+                  addSuggestion id { suggestion }
420+                  throwErrorAt id m!"\
421+`{name}` starts with an uppercase Latin letter, so it denotes an \
422+object-language type here, not the Lean variable `{name}`.
423+
424+This language has no object-language type named `{name}`.
425+Use `~{name}`, or rename the Lean variable to a lowercase/Greek name \
426+such as `τ`."
427+            throwErrorAt id m!"unknown object-language type `{name}`"
428+        | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax
429+    | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax
430+
431+def unsupportedTm : TmElab :=
432+  fun _ _ _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax
433+
434+/-- Handles:
435+* `~` antiquotation
436+* parentheses
437+* arrows
438+* implicit Lean `Ty` antiquotation
439+-/
440+def commonTyHandler (lang : Language) : TyElabHandler :=
441+  fun recur k T => do
442+    match T with
443+    | `(stlcTy| ~$e:term) =>
444+        elabTermEnsuringType e (mkConst lang.tyType)
445+    | `(stlcTy| ($T:stlcTy)) =>
446+        recur T
447+    | `(stlcTy| $A:stlcTy → $B:stlcTy) => do
448+        let A ← recur A
449+        let B ← recur B
450+        return lang.mkArrow A B
451+    | `(stlcTy| $A:stlcTy -> $B:stlcTy) => do
452+        let A ← recur A
453+        let B ← recur B
454+        return lang.mkArrow A B
455+    | `(stlcTy| $id:ident) =>
456+        match classifyIdent? id with
457+        | some (.metavar, _) =>
458+            resolveMetaIdent lang .type (mkConst lang.tyType) id
459+        | some (.object, _) => k T -- handled by downstream
460+        | none => throwErrorAt id "\
461+invalid bare type identifier
462+
463+Use an uppercase Latin identifier for object-language type syntax, \
464+a lowercase/Greek identifier for a Lean type variable, or \
465+explicit `~...` for a Lean expression."
466+    | _ => k T
467+
468+/--
469+Handles:
470+* `~` antiquotation
471+* variables
472+* application
473+* parentheses
474+* lambda
475+* substitution
476+-/
477+def commonTmHandler
478+    (lang : Language)
479+    (elabTy : TyElab) :
480+    TmElabHandler :=
481+  fun recur k Γ free t => do
482+    match t with
483+    -- Explicit ~ antiquotation
484+    | `(stlcTm| ~$e:term) =>
485+        return ( ← elabTermEnsuringType e (mkConst lang.tmType), free)
486+    -- Identifier
487+    | `(stlcTm| $id:ident) =>
488+        match classifyIdent? id with
489+        | some (.metavar, _) => do
490+            let e ← resolveMetaIdent lang .term (mkConst lang.tmType) id
491+            return (e, free)
492+        | some (.object, name) => do
493+            -- 1. Lexically bound object variable.
494+            if let some binding := lookupBinding Γ name then
495+              addBindingInfo id binding
496+              return (lang.mkVar name, free)
497+            -- 2. Existing free object variable.
498+            if let some binding := lookupBinding free name then
499+              addBindingInfo id binding
500+              return (lang.mkVar name, free)
501+            -- 3. First free occurrence.
502+            let binding ← mkSyntheticBinding lang id
503+            addBindingInfo id binding
504+            return (lang.mkVar name, binding :: free)
505+        | none => throwErrorAt id "\
506+invalid bare term identifier
507+
508+Use an uppercase Latin identifier for an object-language variable, \
509+a lowercase/Greek identifier for a Lean term variable, or \
510+explicit `~...` for a Lean expression."
511+
512+    -- Substitution
513+    | `(stlcTm| [$x:stlcVar := $s:stlcTm] $t:stlcTm) => do
514+        let x ← elabStlcVarName lang x
515+        let (s, free) ← recur Γ free s
516+        let (t, free) ← recur Γ free t
517+        return (← lang.mkSubst x s t, free)
518+
519+    -- Application
520+    | `(stlcTm| $f:stlcTm $a:stlcTm) => do
521+        let (f, free) ← recur Γ free f
522+        let (a, free) ← recur Γ free a
523+        return (lang.mkApp f a, free)
524+
525+    -- Parentheses
526+    | `(stlcTm| ($t:stlcTm)) =>
527+        recur Γ free t
528+
529+    -- Lambda
530+    | `(stlcTm| λ $x:stlcVar : $T:stlcTy . $body:stlcTm) => do
531+        let T ← elabTy T
532+        let (x, Γ) ← elabStlcBinder lang Γ x
533+        let (body, free) ← recur Γ free body
534+        return (lang.mkAbs x T body, free)
535+
536+    | _ => k Γ free t
537+
538+
539+abbrev CtxElab := TSyntax `stlcCtx → TermElabM (Expr × Scope)
540+
541+partial def elabCtxCommon
542+    (lang : Language)
543+    (elabTy : TyElab)
544+    (Γ : TSyntax `stlcCtx) :
545+    TermElabM (Expr × Scope) := do
546+  match Γ with
547+  -- Empty object context.
548+  | `(stlcCtx| ∅) => do
549+      return (← lang.mkEmptyCtx, [])
550+  | `(stlcCtx| $id:ident) =>
551+      match classifyIdent? id with
552+      | some (.metavar, _) =>
553+          return (← resolveMetaIdent lang .context lang.ctxType id, [])
554+      | some (.object, name) => do
555+          let ΓTerm : Term := ⟨id.raw⟩
556+          let suggestion ← `(stlcCtx| ~$ΓTerm)
557+          addSuggestion id { suggestion }
558+          throwErrorAt id m!"\
559+`{name}` starts with an uppercase Latin letter, so it denotes an \
560+object-language identifier.
561+
562+Object-language context variables do not exist.
563+Use a lowercase/Greek Lean context variable such as `Γ`, or explicitly \
564+antiquote a Lean context expression using `~...`."
565+      | none => throwErrorAt id "invalid bare context identifier"
566+  -- Dynamic Lean context
567+  | `(stlcCtx| ~$Γ:term) => do
568+      let Γ ← elabTermEnsuringType Γ lang.ctxType
569+      return (Γ, [])
570+  -- Static context extension
571+  | `(stlcCtx| $x:stlcVar ↦ $T:stlcTy ; $Γ:stlcCtx) => do
572+      let (Γ, scope) ← elabCtxCommon lang elabTy Γ
573+      let T ← elabTy T
574+      let (x, scope) ← elabStlcBinder lang scope x
575+      return (← lang.mkExtendCtx Γ x T, scope)
576+  | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax
577+
578+
579+def elabQuoted
580+    (lang : Language)
581+    (elabTy : TyElab)
582+    (elabTm : TmElab)
583+    (elabCtx : CtxElab)
584+    (q : TSyntax `stlcQuoted)
585+    (expectedType? : Option Expr) :
586+    TermElabM Expr := do
587+
588+  let elabOne (q : TSyntax `stlcQuoted) : TermElabM Expr := do
589+    match q with
590+    | `(stlcQuoted| $T:stlcTy) => elabTy T
591+    | `(stlcQuoted| $t:stlcTm) => do
592+        return (← elabTm [] [] t).1
593+    | `(stlcQuoted| $Γ:stlcCtx) => do
594+        return (← elabCtx Γ).1
595+    | `(stlcQuoted| $Γ:stlcCtx ⊢ $t:stlcTm ⦂ $T:stlcTy) => do
596+        let (Γ, scope) ← elabCtx Γ
597+        let (t, _) ← elabTm scope [] t
598+        let T ← elabTy T
599+        lang.mkHasType Γ t T
600+    | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax
601+
602+  let resultType? (q : Syntax) : Option Expr :=
603+    if q.isOfKind ``StlcCommon.quotedTy then
604+      some (mkConst lang.tyType)
605+    else if q.isOfKind ``StlcCommon.quotedTm then
606+      some (mkConst lang.tmType)
607+    else if q.isOfKind ``StlcCommon.quotedCtx then
608+      some lang.ctxType
609+    else if q.isOfKind ``StlcCommon.quotedJudge then
610+      some (mkSort .zero)
611+    else
612+      none
613+
614+  let kindName (stx : Syntax) : String :=
615+    if stx.isOfKind ``StlcCommon.quotedTy then
616+      "type"
617+    else if stx.isOfKind ``StlcCommon.quotedTm then
618+      "term"
619+    else if stx.isOfKind ``StlcCommon.quotedCtx then
620+      "context"
621+    else if stx.isOfKind ``StlcCommon.quotedJudge then
622+      "typing judgment"
623+    else
624+      "unknown"
625+
626+  let alternatives :=
627+    if q.raw.isOfKind choiceKind then
628+      q.raw.getArgs
629+    else
630+      #[q.raw]
631+
632+  let candidates ←
633+    match expectedType? with
634+    | none => pure alternatives
635+    | some expectedType => do
636+      let expectedType ← instantiateMVars expectedType
637+      if expectedType.hasExprMVar then
638+        pure alternatives
639+      else
640+        let mut res := #[]
641+        for alt in alternatives do
642+          if let some resultType := resultType? alt then
643+            if ← isDefEq expectedType resultType then
644+              res := res.push alt
645+        if res.isEmpty then
646+          throwErrorAt q m!"this STLC quotation cannot have the expected Lean type {expectedType}"
647+        pure res
648+
649+  let test (alt : Syntax) : TermElabM Bool := do
650+    let s ← saveState
651+    try
652+      let result? ← commitIfNoErrors? <| elabOne ⟨alt⟩
653+      return result?.isSome
654+    finally
655+      s.restore (restoreInfo := true)
656+
657+  let mut successes := #[]
658+
659+  for alt in candidates do
660+    if ← test alt then
661+      successes := successes.push alt
662+
663+  match successes with
664+  | #[alt] =>
665+      -- Unique interpretation: re-elab it.
666+      elabOne ⟨alt⟩
667+
668+  | #[] =>
669+      -- The expected type selected exactly one category.
670+      -- rerun to get its language-specific error.
671+      if let #[alt] := candidates then
672+        discard <| elabOne ⟨alt⟩
673+
674+      let kinds := candidates.toList
675+        |>.map kindName
676+        |> String.intercalate ", "
677+
678+      throwErrorAt q m!"\
679+this STLC quotation has no valid interpretation
680+
681+Tried: {kinds}
682+
683+Add a Lean type annotation to select an interpretation and obtain a more specific error."
684+
685+  | _ =>
686+      let kinds := successes.toList
687+        |>.map kindName
688+        |> String.intercalate ", "
689+
690+      throwErrorAt q m!"\
691+ambiguous STLC quotation
692+
693+This syntax has multiple valid interpretations:
694+  {kinds}
695+
696+Add a Lean type annotation to select the intended interpretation."
697+
698+end Elab
699+
700+namespace Delab
701+
702+open Lean PrettyPrinter Delaborator SubExpr Parenthesizer Elab
703+
704+@[category_parenthesizer stlcTy]
705+def stlcTy.parenthesizer : CategoryParenthesizer
706+  | prec => do
707+      maybeParenthesize `stlcTy true wrapParens prec <|
708+        parenthesizeCategoryCore `stlcTy prec
709+where
710+  wrapParens (stx : Syntax) : Syntax := Unhygienic.run do
711+    let pstx ← `(stlcTy| ($(⟨stx⟩)))
712+    return pstx.raw.setInfo (SourceInfo.fromRef stx)
713+
714+@[category_parenthesizer stlcTm]
715+def stlcTm.parenthesizer : CategoryParenthesizer
716+  | prec => do
717+      maybeParenthesize `stlcTm true wrapParens prec <|
718+        parenthesizeCategoryCore `stlcTm prec
719+where
720+  wrapParens (stx : Syntax) : Syntax := Unhygienic.run do
721+    let pstx ← `(stlcTm| ($(⟨stx⟩)))
722+    return pstx.raw.setInfo (SourceInfo.fromRef stx)
723+
724+def getTy (stx : Term) : TSyntax `stlcTy :=
725+  withSourceInfoOf (canonical := false) stx <| Unhygienic.run do
726+    match stx with
727+    | `(<{ $T:stlcTy }>) => return T
728+    | `((<{ $T:stlcTy }>)) => return T
729+    | `($id:ident) =>
730+        match classifyIdent? id with
731+        | some (.metavar, _) => `(stlcTy| $id:ident)
732+        | _ => `(stlcTy| ~$stx)
733+    | _ => `(stlcTy| ~$stx)
734+
735+def getTm (stx : Term) : TSyntax `stlcTm :=
736+  withSourceInfoOf (canonical := false) stx <| Unhygienic.run do
737+    match stx with
738+    | `(<{ $t:stlcTm }>) => return t
739+    | `((<{ $t:stlcTm }>)) => return t
740+    | `($id:ident) =>
741+      match classifyIdent? id with
742+      | some (.metavar, _) => `(stlcTm| $id:ident)
743+      | _ => `(stlcTm| ~$stx)
744+    | _ => `(stlcTm| ~$stx)
745+
746+def getVar (stx : Term) : TSyntax `stlcVar :=
747+  withSourceInfoOf (canonical := false) stx <| Unhygienic.run do
748+    match stx with
749+    | `($s:str) =>
750+        let id := mkObjectIdentFrom stx s.getString
751+        match classifyIdent? id with
752+        | some (.object, _) => `(stlcVar| $id:ident)
753+        | _ => `(stlcVar| ~$s)
754+    | _ => `(stlcVar| ~$stx)
755+
756+/-- Each language provides its `reserved` identifiers (to not be printed as ordinary variables) -/
757+def unexpandVar (reserved : String → Bool) (varCtor : Name) : Unexpander
758+  | stx@`($_ $s:str) => do
759+      let name := s.getString
760+      let id := mkObjectIdentFrom stx name
761+      match classifyIdent? id, !reserved name with
762+      | some (.object, _), true =>
763+          let t ← `(stlcTm| $id:ident)
764+          `(<{ $t:stlcTm }>)
765+      | _, _ => pure <| Unhygienic.run do
766+          let var : Term := mkIdentFrom stx varCtor
767+          return (← `($var $s)).raw
768+  | _ => throw ()
769+
770+def delabVar (varCtor : Name) : Delab :=
771+  whenPPOption getPPNotation do
772+    let e ← getExpr
773+    guard <| e.isAppOfArity varCtor 1
774+    match e.appArg! with
775+    | .lit (.strVal _) => failure
776+    | _ => do
777+        let var : Term := mkIdent varCtor
778+        `($var $(← withAppArg delab))
779+
780+def unexpandArrow : Unexpander
781+  | `($_ $A $B) => do
782+      let T ← `(stlcTy| $(getTy A) → $(getTy B))
783+      let q ← `(stlcQuoted| $T:stlcTy)
784+      `(<{ $q:stlcQuoted }>)
785+  | _ => throw ()
786+
787+def unexpandApp : Unexpander
788+  | `($_ $f $a) => do
789+      let t ← `(stlcTm| $(getTm f) $(getTm a))
790+      let q ← `(stlcQuoted| $t:stlcTm)
791+      `(<{ $q:stlcQuoted }>)
792+  | _ => throw ()
793+
794+def unexpandAbs : Unexpander
795+  | `($_ $x $T $t) => `(<{ λ $(getVar x) : $(getTy T) . $(getTm t) }>)
796+  | _ => throw ()
797+
798+def unexpandSubst : Unexpander
799+  | `($_ $x $s $t) => `(<{ [$(getVar x) := $(getTm s)] $(getTm t) }>)
800+  | _ => throw ()
801+
802+partial def unexpandCtx :
803+    Term → UnexpandM (TSyntax `stlcCtx)
804+  | `(∅) => `(stlcCtx| ∅)
805+  | `($x:str →ₚ $T) => do unexpandCtx (← `($x →ₚ $T ; ∅))
806+  | `($x:str →ₚ $T ; $Γ) => do
807+      let Γ' ← unexpandCtx Γ
808+      let x' := getVar x
809+      let T' := getTy T
810+      `(stlcCtx| $x':stlcVar ↦ $T':stlcTy ; $Γ':stlcCtx)
811+  | `($Γ:ident) => `(stlcCtx| $Γ:ident)
812+  | Γ => `(stlcCtx| ~$Γ)
813+
814+def unexpandHasType : Unexpander
815+  | `($_ $Γ $t $T) => do
816+      let Γ' ← unexpandCtx Γ
817+      let t' := getTm t
818+      let T' := getTy T
819+      `(<{ $Γ':stlcCtx ⊢ $t':stlcTm ⦂ $T':stlcTy }>)
820+  | _ => throw ()
821+
822+end Delab
823+
824+end StlcCommon

519---  More technically, a variable `x` *appears free in* a term `t` if `t`
520---  contains some occurrence of `x` that is not under an abstraction
521---  labeled `x`. For example:
522---  - `y` appears free, but `x` does not, in `λx:τ → τ'. x y`
523---  - both `x` and `y` appear free in `(λx:τ → τ'. x y) x`
524---  - no variables appear free in `λx:τ → τ'. λy:τ. x y`
525---
526---  We write this `x ∈ᶠ t`, reading the relation as "`x` is one of the free
527---  variables of `t`". Formally:

949---  Terms do need new productions: a numeral, an infix `*`, and the zero
950---  test. Multiplication binds looser than application and tighter than

952---  associates to the right, so `x * y * z` is `x * (y * z)`.

957---  Instead they are written as though they were functions applied to an

959---  `if0` **is** a keyword, since `then` and `else` leave no other option;

961---  than `if0`, just as the STLC's conditional is `Stlc.Tm.ite`.

754+--  This language uses the shared `<{ ... }>` notation from Stlc. Capital
755+--  Latin identifiers in term positions are `Tm` variables. In type
756+--  positions, `Bool` and `Unit` name the distinguished types above, while
757+--  other capital Latin identifiers, such as `A`, `Int`, or `String`, name
758+--  base types in `Ty`. Lowercase and Greek identifiers refer directly to
759+--  in-scope Lean variables, while arbitrary Lean expressions require `~`
760+--  antiquotation.

768+namespace Elab
769+
770+open StlcCommon
771+open Lean Meta Elab Term
772+
773+
774+def language : Language where
775+  tyType := ``Ty
776+  tmType := ``Tm
777+  arrowCtor := ``Ty.arrow
778+  varCtor := ``Tm.var
779+  appCtor := ``Tm.app
780+  absCtor := ``Tm.abs
781+  -- defined later
782+  subst := `StlcSub.subst
783+  hasType := `StlcSub.HasType
784+
785+def subTyHandler : TyElabHandler :=
786+  fun recur k T => do
787+    match T with
788+    | `(stlcTy| ⊤) => do
789+        return mkConst ``Ty.top
790+    | `(stlcTy| Bool) => do
791+        return mkConst ``Ty.bool
792+    | `(stlcTy| Unit) => do
793+        return mkConst ``Ty.unit
794+    | `(stlcTy| $T₁:stlcTy × $T₂:stlcTy) => do
795+        let T₁ ← recur T₁
796+        let T₂ ← recur T₂
797+        return mkApp2 (mkConst ``Ty.prod) T₁ T₂
798+    | _ => k T
799+
800+/--
801+Make unresolved type identifiers "base types".
802+This must run after `commonTyHandler`
803+so a Lean variable `τ : Ty` is implicitly antiquoted first.
804+-/
805+
806+def baseTyHandler : TyElabHandler :=
807+  fun _recur k T => do
808+    match T with
809+    | `(stlcTy| $id:ident) => do
810+        match classifyIdent? id with
811+        | some (.object, name) =>
812+          return mkApp (mkConst ``Ty.base) (mkStrLit name)
813+        | _ => k T
814+    | _ => k T
815+
816+def tyHandlers : TyElabHandler :=
817+  subTyHandler.orElse ((commonTyHandler language).orElse baseTyHandler)
818+
819+partial def elabTy : TyElab := tyHandlers elabTy  <| unsupportedTy language
820+
821+def subTmHandler : TmElabHandler :=
822+  fun recur k Γ free t => do
823+    match t with
824+    | `(stlcTm| true) =>
825+        return (mkConst ``Tm.tru, free)
826+    | `(stlcTm| false) =>
827+        return (mkConst ``Tm.fls, free)
828+    | `(stlcTm| Bool) =>
829+        throwError "`Bool` is not a valid term."
830+    | `(stlcTm| Unit) =>
831+        throwError "`Unit` is not a valid term."
832+    | `(stlcTm| if $c:stlcTm then $t:stlcTm else $e:stlcTm) => do
833+        let (c, free) ← recur Γ free c
834+        let (t, free) ← recur Γ free t
835+        let (e, free) ← recur Γ free e
836+        return (mkApp3 (mkConst ``Tm.ite) c t e, free)
837+    | `(stlcTm| unit) =>
838+        return (mkConst ``Tm.unit, free)
839+    | `(stlcTm| ($t₁:stlcTm, $t₂:stlcTm)) => do
840+        let (t₁, free) ← recur Γ free t₁
841+        let (t₂, free) ← recur Γ free t₂
842+        return (mkApp2 (mkConst ``Tm.pair) t₁ t₂, free)
843+    | `(stlcTm| fst $t:stlcTm) => do
844+        let (t, free) ← recur Γ free t
845+        return (mkApp (mkConst ``Tm.fst) t, free)
846+    | `(stlcTm| snd $t:stlcTm) => do
847+        let (t, free) ← recur Γ free t
848+        return (mkApp (mkConst ``Tm.snd) t, free)
849+    | _ => k Γ free t
850+
851+def tmHandlers : TmElabHandler := subTmHandler.orElse (commonTmHandler language elabTy)
852+
853+partial def elabTm : TmElab := tmHandlers elabTm unsupportedTm
854+
855+def elabCtx : CtxElab :=
856+  elabCtxCommon language elabTy
857+
858+@[scoped term_elab StlcCommon.bracket]
859+def elabBracket : TermElab :=
860+  fun stx expectedType? => do
861+    let `(<{ $q:stlcQuoted }>) := stx
862+      | throwUnsupportedSyntax
863+    elabQuoted language elabTy elabTm elabCtx q expectedType?
864+
865+end Elab

879+@[app_unexpander Ty.bool]
880+private def Ty.unexpandBool : Unexpander
881+  | stx => do
882+      let Bool := mkObjectIdentFrom stx "Bool"
883+      let T ← `(stlcTy| $Bool:ident)

886+@[app_unexpander Ty.unit]
887+private def Ty.unexpandUnit : Unexpander
888+  | stx => do
889+      let Unit := mkObjectIdentFrom stx "Unit"
890+      let T ← `(stlcTy| $Unit:ident)
891+      `(<{ $T:stlcTy }>)

893+@[app_unexpander Ty.arrow]
894+private def Ty.unexpandArrow : Unexpander := Delab.unexpandArrow

896+@[app_unexpander Ty.prod]
897+private def Ty.unexpandProd : Unexpander
898+  | `($_ $T₁ $T₂) => do
899+      let T₁' := getTy T₁
900+      let T₂' := getTy T₂
901+      `(<{ $T₁':stlcTy × $T₂':stlcTy }>)
902+  | _ => throw ()

904+private def reservedTyNames : String → Bool
905+  | "Bool" | "Unit" => true
906+  | _ => false
907+
908+@[app_unexpander Ty.base]
909+private def Ty.unexpandBase : Unexpander
910+  | stx@`($_ $s:str) => do
911+      let name := s.getString
912+      let id := mkObjectIdentFrom stx name
913+      match classifyIdent? id, reservedTyNames name with
914+      | some (.object, _), false =>
915+          let T ← `(stlcTy| $id:ident)
916+          `(<{ $T:stlcTy }>)
917+      | _, _ => throw ()
918+  | _ => throw ()
919+
920+private def reservedTmNames : String → Bool
921+  | "true" | "false" | "Bool"
922+  | "Unit" | "unit" | "fst"
923+  | "snd" => true
924+  | _ => false
925+
926+

928+private def Tm.unexpandVar : Unexpander :=

931+@[app_delab Tm.var]

933+
934+@[app_unexpander Tm.app]
935+private def Tm.unexpandApp : Unexpander := Delab.unexpandApp

940+@[app_unexpander Tm.tru]
941+private def Tm.unexpandTru : Unexpander

954+@[app_unexpander Tm.ite]

975+      let t₂' := getTm t₂
